recommendation: Keep final-stage roles; add a competing explanation, reciprocal-quote trap with consequences, reconciliation of two records, or a nominal-versus-real policy inference. Preserve the stronger later Legendary tasks.

issue: The correct choice is uniquely qualified or complete in selected AD-AS answer sets.
evidence: Only the key explains both competing mechanisms or both stages. Several alternatives are bare must-shift directions or unrelated-curve claims. This is a structural completeness cue, beyond character count alone.
recommendation: Make each alternative address the same mechanisms/stages and use parallel conditional wording. Keep genuine opposing-shock ambiguity and valid dynamic reasoning. Coordinate any existing D/F task changes before rewriting options.

issue: Three-function answer sets uniquely bundle every action explicitly named in the stem.
evidence: The key lists all three money functions; two alternatives name only one function and the last names reserve requirements/multipliers. Enumeration alone identifies the key.
recommendation: Use four complete ordered mappings of the three actions to functions, with plausible swapped-function errors.

issue: Task type stores an instructional role instead of the question operation.
evidence: type is repair, bridge, checkpoint or mastery_checkpoint even though instructionalRole and challengeStage carry those roles separately.
recommendation: Set type to the actual operation (definition, classification, calculation, graph interpretation, analysis or synthesis); preserve support/boss role and current routing. For questions also being rewritten, set metadata after final wording. Do not change sourceType provenance.

issue: Task-type vocabulary embeds difficulty/checkpoint stages in operation labels.
evidence: Current type values include boss_scaffold_definition, final_boss_graph_diagnosis, legendary_reverse_calculation and similar role-prefixed variants.
recommendation: Remove only stage/role prefixes and map the remaining operation to the existing descriptive task vocabulary. Preserve canonicalDifficulty, instructionalRole and challengeStage; reassess operation after any content rewrite. Historical sourceType remains provenance.

issue: Generated commonError text identifies no item-specific misconception.
evidence: 240 open-economy records use the same direction/accounting sentence; 268 saving/fiscal records substitute a concept label into Uses a neighboring rule instead of the evidence required by....
recommendation: Write a concrete misconception for each current operation: reverse the NCO subtraction, confuse nominal/real quotation, count a bond purchase as capital formation, or infer a behavioral saving shift from an identity, as applicable. Preserve task content and prior economics.

issue: Fourteen integrated Macro questions use unqualified image paths and lack accessible graph descriptions.
evidence: The literal question-assets/<filename> path is absent and not an exact registered asset path. Export resolution finds the corresponding registered concept asset by filename, so PDF images render. imageAlt/graphDescription are absent in these records.
recommendation: Set each image to its exact registered concept-qualified runtimePath; add imageAlt/graphDescription describing visible labels/geometry without giving the answer; set graphRequired for image-dependent tasks. Preserve the verified asset bytes. Verify composer embedding after cleanup; do not characterize the existing PDF as broken.

issue: Sacrifice-ratio feedback supplies one generic algorithm across forward, inverse and policy-comparison questions.
evidence: The same sentence appears in 14 numerical cases, including inverse H-011 and policy comparison DIS-LB-019. It does not show the actual loss/inflation inputs, inverse step or comparison.
recommendation: Explain each requested result with its visible inputs and units. Examples: H-011=9/3=3 percentage points; DIS-LB-019 ratios8/4=2 and4/2.5=1.6. Preserve valid sum-of-annual-gaps conventions.

issue: Generic feedback omits the item-specific calculation, index selection or transmission direction.
evidence: INDEX feedback says only to compare purchasing power even in FB-006, which asks which index to use. MULT-L-001 omits both net effects. MPTX repair says each variable changes without stating directions.
recommendation: Show H-001:1.08/1.05−1=2.9%; L-001:1.15/1.10−1=4.5%; FB-004:54000*240/180=72000, so today is $3000 higher; FB-006 explain consumer versus domestic-output scope. MULT-L-001:300−100=200 versus150−20=130 (after convention adjudication). MPTX:rate falls→investment rises→AD right.

issue: Six Legendary variants repeatedly show the same contractionary graph and ask the same multiplier operation.
evidence: All six keys run MS left→interest rate up→investment down→AD left. Only the stated investment response and MPC change; full-option comparison confirms no new inference.
recommendation: Keep one representative as spaced practice at its calibrated tier. Differentiate the others with reverse inference, an offsetting fiscal change, an expansionary case, a changing MPC comparison, and a transmission constraint. Apply existing D decisions to any unchanged routine variants; do not delete IDs.

issue: Legendary Fisher checkpoint is a numerical clone of the Medium checkpoint.
evidence: LG-Q-3011 uses nominal9, expected3, actual10; LG-Q-9119 uses10,4,11. Both ask who gains and realized real interest, with the same −1% key and identical distractor structure.
recommendation: Preserve the Medium practice. Differentiate Legendary with a fixed-rate versus indexed contract comparison, expected versus realized return reconciliation, or an inverse contract choice. Coordinate its F rewrite once.

issue: Valid integrated tasks are weakened by distractors that deny a supplied mechanism or assert automatic dominance/cancellation.
evidence: NCO-EL-001 turns percentage-point rate changes directly into flow quantities. LPMM-L-004 alternatives say income or price effects always dominate. ICOST alternatives claim indexation stops inflation or causes deflation. AS alternatives omit one of the simultaneous shocks.
recommendation: Retain the integrated task and tier. Replace weak alternatives with complete competing chains: wrong relative return, correct direction but wrong offset, shift-versus-movement confusion, a mistaken nominal/real distinction, or a conditional dominance error. Every choice should engage all material evidence.

issue: Only the correct choice answers both the numerical and identification parts of a two-part question.
evidence: The key gives expected inflation and says what is identified without an offset measurement; all distractors give a number and a false arithmetic assertion but omit the counterfactual identification answer.
recommendation: Retain the advanced task and key. Make all four options contain both an expectation estimate and an explicit statement about identification without the offset, using plausible numerical and underidentification errors.

issue: Feedback describes two curve shifts although the current stem fixes money supply.
evidence: Current stem combines real income rising and price level falling, both shifting money demand in opposite directions. Feedback starts When money demand and money supply both shift....
recommendation: Explain higher real income raises money demand while a lower price level lowers it. With fixed money supply, the net demand and interest-rate direction depend on relative effects.
